title: Siena no. 15: Mario Bandini at the imperial court, Innsbruck, 4 January 1547

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 15; DECODE R4803 (Concistoro_2308_57)
documents.route: Mario Bandini, Sienese orator at the imperial court -> the Signori of Siena

plaintext.source: No decipherment; clear Italian letter around eleven short cipher passages.

transcription.notes: 240 cipher signs plus three Latin-letter code tokens, 8 lines of P2 and 6 of P6; about 65 distinct signs (71 transcription classes). Count from the report, not re-measured. George Lasry names accurate transcription as the main obstacle in this fascicle. The project's own 24 Sept transcription is kept in project_attempt/ and was not used for the reading.

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of Greek-like and invented signs with Latin-letter nomenclator tokens (buf, abs, som, Za) and probable nulls, no word dividers.
system.sibling_key: Filed key R4764 (Buoninsegni, orator to His Majesty) compared by the project on 24 Sept: inconclusive. Compared sign by sign with nos. 17 and 5 (report key figures): a different key.
system.notes: Key figure in key_lasry.jpg (report p. 28); 30 signs listed as unknown.

prior_solution.where: None known; the project's 24 Sept survey left it unread.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry transcribed in CTTS and deciphered part of the cipher with Claude Opus 5.5 by crib guessing and dragging; this project filed his report.

solution.what: Project survey (siena1421): transcription of the P2/P6 runs (agents K, L) and the filed key R4764 compared by sign style; inconclusive, closed as too short.
George Lasry transcribed the cipher passages in CTTS (71 classes).
Crib guessing and dragging with Claude Opus 5.5 inside the clear context.
75 of 240 signs given a value; code words buf, abs, som, Za unidentified.
Report key figures of nos. 15, 17 and 5 compared sign by sign: different keys (Lambda is c here, e in no. 5; theta e here, z in no. 5; square-U n here, i in no. 17).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's partial decipherment and translation (reading.txt, translation.txt, lasry_report.md), his key figure and table; transcription = this project's 24 Sept one (project_attempt/), his CTTS transcription not being in the repository.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading.txt and translation.txt read through; most words carry '?' letters and only a few clauses read whole (5 of 16 sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py). R4803 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method key recovered from ciphertext-only -> not solved; fraction_read 0.3125 -> 0 (75/240 signs kept as key work).

Re-read b35: DECODE R4803 re-fetched (8 images, no attachment); every page opened, P8 is a clear postscript; neighbours R4802, R4804 opened; no decipherment or printed text. Not retried: too short for a ciphertext-only rebuild of the 30 unvalued classes. Kept decoded, not read.

validation.notes: contributed reading: George Lasry's sign-level CTTS transcription and key are not in the repository, so no token alignment can be scored

outcome.method_basis: The report says the passages were partially deciphered by crib guessing and dragging with Claude Opus 5.5; no decipherment or matching filed key exists.

texts.label: No. 15 (R4803), Mario Bandini to the Signori of Siena, Innsbruck, 4 January 1547 (George Lasry's partial reading)
texts.summary: Mario Bandini, Sienese orator at the imperial court, to the Signori of Siena, Innsbruck, 4 January 1547, after the Schmalkaldic campaign: Piergiovanni Salvestri at Innsbruck with the Florentine orator, an occasion to be used and discord in cipher, a minister (Granvelle?) warning that a fire would be kindled in a coded place, and Sienese vases 'all'antica' for Burgundy via Figueroa. Decryption and translation are George Lasry's (75 of 240 signs); the transcription linked is this project's own of 24 Sept 2026, not used in his reading, since his CTTS transcription is not in the repository.
texts.note: Lasry's partial decipherment: question marks inside most words and only a few clauses whole (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026). Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b35, R4803_reread_log.md): DECODE R4803 re-fetched, all 8 images opened (P8 a clear postscript, no decipherment anywhere), neighbours R4802 and R4804 opened; no text exists. About 30 sign classes have no value in 240 signs: too short for a ciphertext-only rebuild; Lasry's CTTS transcription still needed. Kept decoded, not read.
